questions.question: A rectangle is covered exactly by square tiles, with no gaps and no overlaps. Each tile is 1 cm by 1 cm. There are 3 rows of tiles, and each row has 5 tiles, and every tile is shaded. What is the area of the rectangle?
options: 15 cm²
8 cm²
16 cm
15 cm
questions.explain: Area is how many 1 cm squares cover the shape: 3 rows of 5 tiles is 15 tiles, so 15 cm². The 16 comes from going around the outside, which is perimeter, not area.

questions.question: A grid has 4 rows with 4 squares in each row, and every square is 1 cm by 1 cm, so 16 squares in all. Nine of them, forming a 3 by 3 block in one corner, are shaded green. What is the area of the green part?
options: 12 cm²
9 cm²
16 cm²
7 cm²
questions.explain: Count the shaded unit squares: 9 squares of 1 cm² each give an area of 9 cm². Tracing around the outside of the green block gives 12 cm, which is its perimeter, not its area.

questions.question: The floor of a garden shed is covered exactly by square tiles that are each 1 m by 1 m. There are 2 rows of tiles, and each row has 6 tiles. What is the area of the floor?
options: 8 m²
12 m²
questions.explain: Each tile covers 1 m², and 2 rows of 6 tiles is 12 tiles, so the area is 12 m². Walking around the edge of the floor gives 16 m, which measures perimeter — a length, not a covering.

questions.question: A shape is drawn on a grid made of 1 cm by 1 cm squares. Ben says the area of the shape is 7 cm². What does that tell you about the shape?
options: A piece of string 7 cm long fits exactly around the outside of the shape.
Exactly 7 squares, each 1 m by 1 m, cover the shape.
The shape is 7 cm long from one side to the other.
Exactly 7 of the 1 cm by 1 cm grid squares cover the shape.
questions.explain: cm² means square centimetres: the number of 1 cm by 1 cm squares needed to cover a shape. A string around the outside would be measured in plain cm and gives the perimeter instead.

questions.question: Jasmine outlines a rectangle on a 1 cm grid. Exactly 24 grid squares fit inside her outline, and a piece of string 20 cm long goes exactly once around the outline. Which statement is true?
options: The area is 24 cm², because 24 squares of 1 cm² cover the inside.
The area is 44 cm², because you use both numbers.
The area is 20 cm², because the string measures 20.
The area is 24 cm and the perimeter is 20 cm².
questions.explain: Area counts the squares that cover the inside, so it is 24 cm²; the string around the outside measures the perimeter, 20 cm. Grabbing the 'around' number for area is the most common slip.

questions.question: Mr. Dhillon wants to report the area of the school gym floor. Which unit makes the most sense for that measurement?
options: metres (m)
square metres (m²)
square centimetres (cm²)
centimetres (cm)
questions.explain: Area is always in square units, and a gym floor is large, so count 1 m by 1 m squares and write m². Plain metres measure lengths, like the distance around the gym, which is perimeter.

questions.question: Nina is gluing felt onto the top of a rectangular pencil box so that the whole top is covered. To find out how much felt to buy, what should she measure, and how?
options: The perimeter — count the centimetres all the way around the edge of the top.
The perimeter — count the 1 cm squares that fit around the outside edge only.
The area — count how many 1 cm by 1 cm squares cover the whole top, and write the answer in cm².
The length of the longest side of the top, in cm.
questions.explain: Covering a surface is an area question, so count the 1 cm squares that fit on the top and answer in cm². Measuring around the edge gives perimeter, which would only tell her how much ribbon to run around the border.

questions.question: A soccer practice patch at Riley's school is covered exactly by square pieces of turf that are each 1 m by 1 m. There are 9 rows with 7 pieces in each row. How much turf covers the patch?
options: 32 m²
16 m²
63 m²
questions.explain: Each piece of turf covers 1 m², and 9 rows of 7 pieces is 63 pieces, so 63 m². The 32 is the distance around the patch in metres — perimeter — which would only tell you how much line to paint around the edge.

questions.question: Ella's bedroom floor is covered exactly by square mats that are each 1 m by 1 m: 4 rows with 3 mats in each row. Her brother walks once around the very edge of the floor, counting 14 steps of 1 m, and says 'So the floor is 14 m² of mats.' Which answer is correct?
options: 12 m², because 12 mats of 1 m² cover the floor; his 14 m is only the perimeter.
7 m², because 4 + 3 = 7 tells you how many mats fit along the two sides of the floor.
14 m², because he counted every metre of the floor when he stepped around it.
14 m, because the distance he walked is exactly how much floor there is to cover.
questions.explain: Area is how many 1 m squares cover the floor: 4 rows of 3 mats is 12 mats, so 12 m². Walking around the edge measures perimeter, 14 m, which is a distance and not the amount of floor covered.

questions.question: The reading corner in a Grade 5 classroom is covered with carpet squares that are each 1 m by 1 m: 6 rows with 4 squares in each row. Three of those squares are lifted out to make room for a bookshelf. What area of carpet is left on the floor?
options: 24 m², because that is the size of the whole corner before anything was moved.
21 m², because 24 squares covered the corner and 3 of them were taken out.
20 m², because it is 20 m around the outside of the corner, so 20 squares fit.
27 m², because 24 + 3 = 27 once you count the 3 lifted squares as well.
questions.explain: First count the covering squares, 6 rows of 4 is 24 m², then subtract the 3 that were removed to get 21 m². The 20 is the distance around the corner — perimeter — which does not tell you how much carpet there is.

questions.question: Two decks are built from square boards that are each 1 m by 1 m. Deck A is 2 boards wide and 8 boards long. Deck B is 4 boards wide and 4 boards long. Which statement is true?
options: Deck A covers more, because it takes 20 m of railing to go around it and Deck B only takes 16 m.
Deck B covers more, because a square always covers more than a long thin shape.
Both decks cover the same area, 16 m² each, even though the distance around them is different.
Deck A covers 20 m² and Deck B covers 16 m².
questions.explain: Count the boards that cover each deck: 2 × 8 = 16 and 4 × 4 = 16, so both areas are 16 m². The 20 m and 16 m are perimeters — a longer edge around a shape does not mean more area inside it.

questions.question: Mr. Fraser's patio in Kamloops is covered exactly by square stones that are each 1 m by 1 m: 8 rows with 3 stones in each row. His neighbour adds up the sides — 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 — and says the patio must be 22 m² of stone. Which answer is correct?
options: 22 m², because adding all four sides gives the amount of stone on the patio.
11 m², because 8 + 3 = 11 counts one long side and one short side of the patio.
22 m, because the distance all the way around the patio is how much patio there is.
24 m², because 24 stones of 1 m² cover the patio; the 22 m is only the perimeter.
questions.explain: Area is how many 1 m squares cover the patio: 8 rows of 3 stones is 24 stones, so 24 m². Adding the sides, 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 m, walks around the edge — that is the perimeter, a distance and not a covering — and 8 + 3 = 11 only adds two of the sides.
